paper_sections.title: The Temporal Dynamics of Voluntary Emotion Regulation
Modulation of the sustained by the immediate aftereffect

description.value: The study investigated the immediate and delayed neural aftereffects of voluntary emotion regulation by detachment, focusing on amygdala responses during active regulation and during passive viewing of the same aversive stimuli approximately ten minutes later.

design.value: Healthy female volunteers completed two sequenced fMRI tasks: an active emotion regulation task using negative and neutral visual scenes, followed approximately ten minutes later by passive viewing of the same stimuli in a newly randomized order. A separate independent sample completed a behavioral control experiment with trial-by-trial affect ratings.

description.value: Subjects completed versions of the Beck Depression Inventory in order to rule out effects of altered mood states.
Subjects completed versions of the State Trait Anxiety Inventory in order to rule out effects of altered mood states.
Subjects completed the Toronto Alexithymia Scale to rule out effects of deficits in emotion perception.
The Emotion Regulation Questionnaire was used to test for the influence of habitual emotion regulation strategies on potential aftereffects; suppression and reappraisal subscale scores were reported.
The White Bear Suppression Inventory was used as a measure of habitual thought control and to test whether it modulated potential aftereffects.
Emotion regulation success was rated post-hoc on a 9-point Likert scale, where 1 was very successful and 9 was not successful.

description.value: 20 healthy right-handed female volunteers, 24±3 years, without any history of neurological or psychiatric illness participated in the imaging study. Two subjects reached BDI scores above the cut-off score of 9 and thus were discarded from further analyses; 18 subjects were included in the analyses.

description.value: An independent sample (n=10) participated in a control experiment using a trial-by-trial rating of subjective negative affect.

task_description.value: Subjects saw 60 pictures of negative or neutral content taken from the International Affective Picture System. They were instructed either to simply watch the pictures and permit all upcoming emotions or to intentionally regulate their emotions by taking the position of a neutral observer. The cue word was presented for 2 s, pictures were presented for 8 s, and subjects then relaxed for 20 s without regulating any more. Trials were presented in randomized order, and task 1 was performed in two consecutive sessions of 15 minutes each.

instructions.value: “Look at the following picture directly but try to take the position of a noninvolved observer, thinking about the present picture in a neutral way” for the regulation condition or “Look at the following picture directly and permit feeling your emotions” for the no-regulation condition.

stimuli.value: 60 pictures of negative or neutral content taken from the International Affective Picture System and matched for complexity and content of faces, scenery, food and nature.

task_performance_measures.value: Post-hoc emotion regulation success rated on a 9-point Likert scale.

task_description.value: Approximately ten minutes after the end of task 1, subjects were instructed to just look at the 60 pictures from the IAPS again. The pictures were presented for only 1 s each in a newly randomized order, with a 3 s intertrial interval and variable jitter within ±1 TR, minimizing intentional emotion regulation efforts.

instructions.value: Subjects were instructed to just look at the pictures; no instructions to regulate were given.

stimuli.value: The same 60 negative and neutral pictures from the IAPS used in task 1.

task_description.value: An independent sample of 10 subjects completed a control experiment using a trial-by-trial rating of subjective negative affect to confirm the success of the emotion regulation procedure.

task_performance_measures.value: Trial-by-trial rating of subjective negative affect, from 0 (weakest) to 7 (strongest).

instrument.value: 3 Tesla Siemens Allegra scanner equipped with a head coil

description.value: T2* weighted functional MR images were obtained using event-related echoplanar imaging in a tangential-axial orientation. Image size was 64×64 pixels, with a field of view of 192 mm and a flip angle of 90°. One whole-brain volume consisted of 31 slices. Slice thickness was 3 mm with a 25% gap, resulting in a voxel size of 3×3×3.75 mm. Volumes were obtained every 2000 ms with TE 35 ms.

instrument.value: 3 Tesla Siemens Allegra scanner equipped with a head coil

description.value: Functional MR images were acquired with the same parameters as task 1 except that volumes were obtained every 1500 ms and one volume consisted of 23 slices with a slice thickness of 3 mm and a 25% gap, covering the brain from the temporal poles to the superior parietal cortex and including the amygdala, prefrontal and parietal cortex.

description.value: For each subject, three-dimensional T1 weighted anatomical volumes were acquired.
Data preprocessing included realignment, spatial normalization to the EPI-template and spatial smoothing.

steps.value: spatial normalization to the EPI-template (2×2×2 mm)

model_settings.value: The regression model consisted of five regressors: instruction, non-regulated negative, non-regulated neutral, regulated negative, and regulated neutral, plus six regressors describing residual motion. Intrinsic autocorrelations were accounted for by an autoregressive model of 1 order and low frequency drifts were removed via high pass filter.

In a second level random effects group analysis, individual regionally specific effects of conditions for each subject were compared using a within-subject ANOVA with a 2×2 design with the factors regulation condition (regulation, no regulation) and valence (negative, neutral), with non-sphericity correction.
The mean time course for each subject and each condition was included in an ANOVA for repeated measures with the factors valence, regulation and period. Data were taken from scan 5 and scan 9.

Regression analysis on extracted individual data for the contrast regulation negative>no-regulation negative in DLPFC with the contrast no-regulation negative>regulation negative in left and right amygdala.

Simple regression analyses tested correlations between individual WBSI scores and the immediate aftereffect, and between amygdala activation during presentation of formerly regulated negative pictures in task 2 and individual differences in peak immediate aftereffect magnitude in task 1.
